data.summary_en: The 60 monopile foundations designed and installed by MT Højgaard began to fail in April 2010, with transition pieces slipping down the monopiles; the cause was an error in the DNV J101 standard that over-estimated axial capacity by a factor of about ten, as had already shown at Egmond aan Zee a year earlier. Who bears the EUR 26.25m remedial cost went to the UK Supreme Court, which found for E.ON in August 2017 (UKSC 2017/59).

data.summary_en: A year after the world's first large offshore wind farm started, the dry-type transformers of its 80 Vestas V80s began failing (from summer 2003) and production defects were then found in many generators; with repairs hampered by North Sea conditions, Vestas announced on 9 July 2004 that all 80 nacelles plus the Tjæreborg test nacelle (81) would be shipped to Ringkøbing and Lem for repair, to finish in the autumn.

data.summary_en: At about 20:00 CEST on 24 April the cargo ship Petra L hit a 6 MW turbine at Gode Wind 1 inside the German EEZ, then sailed to Emden under her own power with a 5 × 3 m hole in the starboard hull and water ingress; the turbine returned to service about 24 hours after inspection. Germany's BSU investigated it as a serious marine casualty and published report 192/23 in January 2025.

sources.quote: A wind turbine at the Scroby Sands offshore wind farm in the UK caught fire yesterday morning (15 August). The cause of the fire, which self-extinguished later the same day, is now being investigated.
RWE, the wind farm’s owner, said the fire broke out in the nacelle and that no one was working on board the wind turbine at the time, with the fire later extinguishing on its own.
HM Coast Guard reports it was notified of the fire at 10:50 am local time as residents on the coast watched and filmed the fire at the nearshore location.

data.summary_en: At 10:50 on 15 August the Coastguard was alerted to a nacelle fire on one of the 30 × 2 MW turbines at Scroby Sands, visible from the shore; no one was on board and the fire burned itself out the same day while RWE investigated (offshoreWIND.biz 16 Aug 2023). The gutted turbine was only scheduled for removal two years later.

data.summary_en: On 12 January a 110 m turbine at the 19-year-old 72 × 2.3 MW farm dropped off the grid and was found the next day lying in the sea together with its concrete gravity-base foundation (about 2,050 t in all); nobody was present or hurt. sources.quote: The Sheng Ping 001 jack-up vessel, formerly Teras Fortress 2, tilted on 25 July while working at the site of China General Nuclear Power Corporation’s (CGN) wind farm off Huizhou, with four people reported missing
Of the total of 65 people on board, 61 were evacuated from the site and transferred to shore the same day, while four went missing.
At the time of the capsizing, the jackup was involved in the final stages of construction of CGN's Huizhou Gangkou I wind farm, which will have a generating capacity of 400 MW once completed.

data.title_zh: 自升式安裝船「升平 001」傾斜進水，4 人落海失蹤
data.title_en: Jack-up Sheng Ping 001 tilted and flooded; four people lost overboard
data.summary_zh: 7 月 25 日上午約 11 時，為中廣核惠州港口一（400 MW）施工的自升式安裝船升平 001（前 Teras Fortress 2）作業中傾斜進水，船上 65 人中 61 人當天撤離、4 人落海失蹤，40 多艘船隻與直升機搜救，27 日晚間仍未尋獲（offshoreWIND.biz 2021-07-26、07-28 引述央視）。
data.summary_en: At about 11:00 on 25 July the jack-up Sheng Ping 001 (ex Teras Fortress 2), working on CGN's 400 MW Huizhou Gangkou I, tilted and flooded; 61 of the 65 on board were evacuated the same day and four went overboard and missing, with more than 40 vessels and helicopters searching and no one found by the night of 27 July (offshoreWIND.biz 26 and 28 Jul 2021 citing CCTV).
data.cap_note_zh: 港口一期 400 MW（本站紀錄一、二期合計 1,000 MW）
data.cas_zh: 央視：4 人失蹤（後續未查到官方結果）
data.cas_en: CCTV: four missing (no official outcome found)
data.verify_zh: 媒體報導核對（出處原文已以 check_quotes 核對）
data.note_zh: 媒體推測為樁腿穿刺（punch-through），官方未公布，不填原因；死亡人數待官方確認。
data.note_en: Press speculated a leg punch-through; nothing official, cause left blank; fatalities await official confirmation.

sources.quote: Ofgem has concluded that two large power stations, Hornsea One Ltd (co-owned by Orsted) and Little Barford (operated by RWE) did not remain connected after the lightning strike.
They have agreed to make a voluntary payment of £4.5 million each into Ofgem’s redress fund.
triggered the subsequent disconnection, loss of power and disruption to more than one million consumers.

data.title_zh: 雷擊後風場未保持併網，英國百萬用戶大停電
data.title_en: Farm failed to ride through a lightning strike; over a million UK customers cut off
data.summary_zh: 8 月 9 日輸電線路遭雷擊後，Hornsea One（當時仍在安裝、174×7 MW）與 Little Barford 燃氣電廠都未保持併網，合計出力驟降觸發低頻卸載，逾百萬用戶停電、鐵路大亂；Ofgem 調查認定兩者違反併網規範，Hornsea One Ltd 與 RWE 各自願支付 450 萬英鎊（Ofgem 2020-01-03）。
data.summary_en: After lightning hit a transmission line on 9 August, Hornsea One (174 × 7 MW, still being installed) and the Little Barford gas plant both failed to stay connected; the combined loss triggered low-frequency load shedding that cut off more than a million customers and disrupted rail services. Ofgem found both had breached their connection obligations and each made a voluntary £4.5 million payment (Ofgem 3 Jan 2020).
data.cap_note_zh: 174×7 MW；Ofgem 稱出力由 799 MW 降至 62 MW（報導：失去 2、3 模組共 737 MW）
data.verify_zh: 主管機關／業主一手資料
data.note_zh: 跨系統事件；風機控制器對電壓波動反應錯誤的技術細節見 Ofgem 調查報告。
data.note_en: A system-wide event; the turbine-controller voltage-response detail is in Ofgem's investigation report.

data.area_zh: 奧勒岡州 Sherman 郡 Wasco
data.title_zh: 維修後煞車放開風機飛車，葉片擊塔倒塌，1 死 1 傷
data.title_en: Overspeed after maintenance; a blade struck the tower and it collapsed, killing one worker
data.summary_zh: 施工收尾中的 Klondike III（44×2.3 MW Siemens＋80×1.5 MW GE）一部 Siemens 風機 8 月 25 日倒塌，塔頂的 Siemens 技師 Chadd Mitchell 死亡、塔內另 1 人受傷。奧勒岡 OSHA 調查：技師進輪轂後把葉片轉到最大受風位置並鎖住隔離裝置，離開時未復位，放開服務煞車後風力使轉子飛車、葉片擊中塔架；無結構缺陷，罰 Siemens 10,500 美元（OSHA 2008-03）。美國風電首起工人死亡事故之一。
data.summary_en: On 25 August a Siemens turbine at Klondike III (44 × 2.3 MW Siemens plus 80 × 1.5 MW GE, nearing completion) collapsed, killing Siemens technician Chadd Mitchell at the top and injuring another worker inside. Oregon OSHA found no structural defect: a technician had set the blades to maximum wind resistance and closed the pitch isolation devices, left them that way, and when the service brake was released the out-of-position blades drove the rotor into overspeed and a blade struck the tower; Siemens was fined $10,500 (OSHA, March 2008).
data.owner: PPM Energy（今 Avangrid）；風機當時仍屬 Siemens

sources.quote: All proceeded normally until 3:10 in the morning of March 26. That's when disaster struck the turbine. Turning in a 20-mph wind, one of the 75-foot blades suddenly snapped off and hurled off into space.
The 1.25 MW turbine operated for 1100 hours before a blade failed at a known weak point, which had not been reinforced due to wartime material shortages.
Repairs were never done after the March 1945 failure. The prototype turbine was dismantled in 1946, leaving only concrete footings and a marker plaque at the site

data.area_zh: 佛蒙特州 Castleton 附近 Grandpa's Knob
data.title_zh: 世界首部百萬瓦級風機葉片斷裂，計畫就此結束
data.title_en: The first megawatt-class turbine lost a blade and the project ended
data.summary_zh: 1941 年併網的 1.25 MW 兩葉式 Smith–Putnam 風機累積運轉約 1,100 小時後，1945 年 3 月 26 日凌晨 3:10 在 20 mph 風中一片 8 噸、75 呎長的葉片自葉根斷裂飛出（翼梁舊裂縫延伸，戰時材料短缺未能徹底補強），落在山坡 700 呎外；未再修復，1946 年拆除（Rutland Herald；維基百科）。
data.summary_en: The 1.25 MW two-bladed Smith–Putnam turbine, grid-connected in 1941, had run about 1,100 hours when at 3:10 am on 26 March 1945, in a 20 mph wind, one 8-ton, 75 ft blade snapped at the root (an old crack in the spar had grown; wartime shortages had prevented full reinforcement) and landed 700 ft down the slope; it was never repaired and was dismantled in 1946 (Rutland Herald; Wikipedia).
data.turbine: S. Morgan Smith／Putnam 1.25 MW 兩葉下風式
data.owner: S. Morgan Smith Company（售電給 Central Vermont Public Service）

data.note_zh: Mills Archive 寫 3 月 25 日；本列採 Rutland Herald 的 3 月 26 日 3:10。
data.note_en: Mills Archive gives 25 March; this row follows the Rutland Herald (3:10 am, 26 March).

sources.quote: When it was decommissioned it had only logged a total of 420 hours in active operation.
Growian was decommissioned over the course of 1987, and dismantled in summer 1988.
In the end Growian cost nearly twice that estimated and was dismantled from 1987 to 1988.

data.area_zh: 什勒斯維希－霍爾斯坦邦 Kaiser-Wilhelm-Koog
data.title_zh: 世界最大 3 MW 試驗風機只運轉 420 小時即除役
data.title_en: The world's largest 3 MW test turbine was retired after only 420 operating hours
data.summary_zh: 1983 年投入測試的 3 MW、葉輪直徑 100 公尺兩葉下風式 Growian 因多項嚴重設計缺陷無法持續試運轉，1987 年 8 月停止運作時只累積 420 小時發電，1987 年除役、1988 年夏拆除，造價近估算的兩倍（維基百科；wind-works.org）。被視為風電史上最大的失敗案例之一，但 25 年後同尺寸機型成為市場主流。
data.summary_en: The 3 MW, 100 m rotor, two-bladed downwind Growian, tested from 1983, could not sustain test operation because of serious design faults; when it stopped in August 1987 it had logged only 420 hours, was decommissioned in 1987 and dismantled in summer 1988 at nearly twice the estimated cost (Wikipedia; wind-works.org). Regarded as one of wind power's great failures, though turbines of the same size dominated the market 25 years later.
